basis: Skeletal deformities and joint contractures define disease; thickened, inelastic skin occurs in 80-99%. Palpebral dysmorphism alone does not establish ocular damage.
Amyloid protein deposition causes progressive renal dysfunction. Hepatic and pulmonary deposits are common, but functional injury is not established in >=30%.
Developmental brain malformation with severe intellectual disability, spasticity and seizures; associated cardiac and ocular abnormalities lack evidence of common involvement.
Disease of ocular blood vessels; conjunctival versus corneal wording does not change the affected axes.
Extranodal lymphoid malignancy arising in the esophagus; gastrointestinal origin and both lymphoma mechanism axes apply.
Carcinoma confined to cutaneous epithelium.
Villous adenocarcinoma most commonly denotes intestinal carcinoma associated with villous adenoma; site-unspecified definition and gynecologic subtypes limit certainty.
Inherited susceptibility specifically to acute lymphoblastic leukemia; haematologic axis identifies the defining disease target, without assuming active leukemia.
Carcinoma arising in the uterine ligament, a reproductive structure outside the axes.
Symptomatic abnormal positioning of the colon; proximity to liver and diaphragm does not imply damage to either.
Inherited dicarboxylate transport disorder causing biochemical abnormalities and cerebral white-matter dysfunction; urinary metabolites do not establish renal damage.
Progressive central and peripheral neurologic disease; fixed pes cavus and neurogenic bladder each occur in 30-79%. Gaze abnormalities reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Melanoma originating in the posterior uvea; metastatic disease is not intrinsic organ involvement.
Secondary systemic hypertension; the unspecified underlying cause and later target-organ complications are separate conditions.
Ovarian germ-cell malignancy; reproductive origin does not establish endocrine gland dysfunction.
Inherited vitamin A metabolic disorder; night blindness and Bitot spots are characteristic ocular deficiency manifestations, with frequency unspecified. Skin frequency is unclear.
Viral infection defined by reactivation; this umbrella does not establish common lasting injury to a particular anatomical organ.
Carcinoma confined to the ureter, which belongs to the renal axis.
Cold-triggered autoinflammatory disease; rash, conjunctivitis and arthralgia are usually transient. Renal amyloidosis occurs in 1/26; isolated uveitis reports lack robust frequency.
ADCY5-related neurologic movement disorder; orofacial movements do not establish oral tissue or skeletal muscle damage.
Structural aneurysmal abnormality of the myocardial wall.
Ischemic necrosis of heart muscle; coronary thrombosis remains within the cardiovascular axis.
HSF4-related nonsyndromic lens cataract.
Defined by structural and functional brain injury associated with diabetes; the underlying diabetes is a separate disease.
Hormone resistance and AHO skeletal defects define disease; intellectual disability and cataract each 30-79%. Subcutaneous ossification and dental defects omitted at cap.
